relations.rationale: Ana's class membership has no bearing on when the group took a break.
Ana being in Esme's class doesn't determine whether Ana is in Lena's class, unless Esme and Lena are known to be in different classes, which isn't stated.
Class membership has nothing to do with relative ages between Vik and Esme.
Splitting into pairs to cover ground is consistent with and plausibly explains careful movement around hazards, though not a strict logical link.
Splitting into pairs has no bearing on relative heights of Finn and Vik.
The group splitting into pairs is consistent with and sets up the possibility of a Finn-Vik pairing being efficient.
Pairing up for ground-covering has no bearing on class membership.
Splitting into pairs earlier doesn't determine whether the group later gathered and left together.
Careful movement around tide pools doesn't imply anything about a later break.
Careful movement around hazards doesn't directly indicate cleanliness progress, though it's plausibly part of a cleanup effort.
Height comparison doesn't determine walking speed comparison.
Finn being taller than Vik doesn't affect whether their pairing was efficient at hauling bags.
Vik being faster could complement Finn's pace, plausibly making their pairing efficient for hauling tasks.
Walking speed comparison is unrelated to sharing snacks during a break.
Vik's walking speed relative to Finn has no bearing on the beach's cleanliness by afternoon.
Walking speed comparison is unrelated to the arrangement of sorted recyclables.
Walking speed has no bearing on relative ages.
Efficiency of a work pairing has no bearing on class membership.
The efficiency of Finn and Vik's pairing has no bearing on whether Lena is the youngest.
An efficient pairing during work doesn't determine whether everyone later left together at sunset.
